newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: Libya rejects UN criticism of unapproved flight.
newsitem.headline: Libya rejects UN criticism of unapproved flight.

text.p: Libya on Wednesday rejected the Security Council's criticism of a recent flight by a Libyan aircraft taking pilgrims from Tripoli to Saudi Arabia in defiance of U.N. sanctions.

Referring to a statement the council issued at a meeting last Friday, Libyan U.N. envoy Abuzed Dorda said in a letter to the council president that the pilgrimage to Mecca was a religious duty for Moslems and did not require authorisation.

"Its performance and the choice of a means of reaching the Holy Places is one of the rights of a Moslem on which there are no religious restrictions and with respect to which he does not require anyone's intercession or permission," Dorda said.

Libya has been subject to mandatory U.N. sanctions including an air embargo since 1992 for failing to extradite two men charged in Britain and the United States with involvement in the 1988 mid-air bombing of Pan Am flight 103 over Lockerbie, Scotland, which killed 270 people.

This was the third year in a row Libya had violated the sanctions by flying pilgrims to Jeddah on an unauthorised flight even though the council gave permission for an Egyptian plane to ferry Libyans wishing to make the annual pilgrimage.

Dorda conveyed Libya's "deep concern and regret that such a statement should have been adopted by the Security Council." Libya would have expected it to be "more perceptive in addressing religious issues that concern a person's faith and his relationship with his God ... and because of the political repercussions of encroaching upon this relationship."

He said the council should "refrain from interfering in this sensitive religious matter out of respect for the right of Moslems to perform their rites and in order to avoid the complications that might ensue from provoking the sentiments not only of Moslems in my country but also of Moslems in general."
